useCase.name: Declare the day the school holds its parent-teacher meeting, cancel the teaching for it, and notify everyone

intent.name: meetingday.declare
intent.summary: Declare the day of the school-wide parent-teacher meeting, and send it to the Principal for approval.

request.gloss: mark it in the calendar now

routesElsewhere.note: That is the everyday case, and it carries a slot the teacher chooses. This declares a day for everybody.

request.gloss: put it on the website as well

routesElsewhere.note: Publishing the meeting on the school website is a separate act, and whether the school does it at all is an open question here (OQ-5).

steps.note: One step, and it stops at the Principal. The declaration is checked against the calendar and reports how many lectures will not run, but nothing is marked and nobody is told (BR-2, AC-1).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A date the school is already closed on, a date in the past, a window that ends before it begins, no class or no place to attend — each refuses the declaration and none of them half-declares it.
plan.atomicity: One write: the declaration, awaiting the Principal. Nothing else happens — the calendar is untouched, every lecture still stands, attendance is still expected and no teacher or guardian has been told (BR-2, E6, AC-1).

planningRules.rule: Never widen the classes. A class added to the declaration loses a day's teaching and a day's attendance, and a class left off teaches as normal — the difference is the whole design (BR-1, BR-6, AC-8).
Never write where families are to come. It is the school's own wording, it goes out with the notification, and a family told the date but not the door arrives at the wrong gate (BR-7, E5).
Report the lectures that would stop before anybody approves anything. That is what the Principal is approving — not a date, but a day of teaching cancelled for those classes (BR-4, AC-3).
Say that nothing has happened yet. A declaration submitted is not a meeting declared: the calendar is untouched, the lectures still stand and no family has been told (BR-2, E6, AC-1).

Name the teachers who would be in two places. A teacher holding a lecture that day for a class not taking part still has to teach it, and nothing here resolves the clash with the meeting window (BR-6, OQ-2).

Never offer to hold it outside teaching hours as a way of keeping the lectures. The declaration always suspends the day's lectures for the classes taking part, and whether the school could do otherwise is unanswered (OQ-3).

reversal.statement: Nothing has to be undone, because nothing was done. A declaration the Principal does not approve is returned with a reason, and the calendar, the timetable, the attendance and every family are exactly as they were (BR-2, A2).

steps.note: One step with five consequences: the day is marked for those classes alone, their lectures stop, no cover is raised, no attendance is expected, and the teachers and guardians are told (BR-3, BR-4, BR-5, BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Nothing is marked before the approval is recorded, and a notification that fails is reported rather than assumed — a family not told arrives on an ordinary day, or does not arrive at all.
plan.atomicity: One act with five effects, and they hold together or not at all: the calendar marking for the classes taking part, the lectures suspended with no substitution cover raised (BR-4, E7), the attendance expectation removed (BR-5, E8, E9), the teachers notified and the guardians notified (BR-7). A partial application leaves a day that teaches nothing and marks everybody absent.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Declared.

fields.description: The Principal. The School Admin who declared it cannot approve it (BR-2).

fields.description: The classes the day is marked for. It is not a school-wide closure (BR-3, AC-2).

fields.name: lectures_suspended
fields.description: Lectures that will not run, with no substitution cover raised for any of them (BR-4, E7, AC-4).

fields.name: attendance_suspended_for
fields.description: Classes for which no record is expected that day. No student is marked absent, no absence alert is sent, and the day counts in no attendance percentage and in no chronic absence figure (BR-5, E8, E9, AC-5, AC-6, AC-7).

fields.name: classes_unaffected
fields.description: Classes not taking part. Their lectures run and their attendance is taken as on any other day (BR-6, AC-8).

fields.name: teachers_notified
fields.description: Teachers holding the suspended lectures, told which of their lectures will not run (BR-7).

fields.name: guardians_notified
fields.description: Guardians of students in the classes taking part, told the date, the window and where to attend (BR-7, AC-9).

fields.name: unreachable_guardians
fields.description: Guardians the messaging module could not reach. They will not know the day has changed and will send their children as usual.

fields.name: staff_attendance_unchanged
fields.description: True. Nothing here decides whether a meeting day is a working day for staff attendance, and the use case does not say (OQ-1).

errors.meaning: The acting user is not the Principal.
errors.notWritten: Nothing is marked, no lecture is suspended and nobody is told.
errors.note: The School Admin declares and cannot approve (BR-2), but the use case writes no exception for the attempt — its only approval exception is E6, which is about the calendar being marked rather than about who acts.

planningRules.rule: Say what approving does before it is done. It is not a sign-off — it cancels a day of teaching for those classes, suspends their attendance, and messages every guardian in them at once (BR-2, BR-3, BR-7).
Never let it read as a school closure. The day is marked for the classes taking part alone; a class not taking part teaches as normal and its attendance is taken (BR-3, BR-6, AC-8).

Say that the day counts against nobody. No record is expected, no student is marked absent, no absence alert goes out, and the day is excluded from every attendance percentage and from the chronic absence figures — a day nobody was asked to attend must not count against anybody (BR-5, AC-7).

Say that no substitution cover is raised. A teacher meeting parents is not absent from a lecture that is not happening, and cover raised for one would put a substitute in an empty room (BR-4, E7, AC-4).
Report the guardians the messaging module could not reach. They will send their children on a day the school is not teaching them, and nothing else in this use case notices (BR-7, AC-9).
Never claim anything about staff attendance. Teachers attend, but whether a meeting day is a working day for them is an open question the use case raises and does not answer (OQ-1).

reversal.statement: The reversal has to be complete: cancelling restores the timetable for that day, unmarks the calendar, restores the attendance expectation and notifies everybody who was told (BR-9, AC-11). A partial reversal leaves a day that teaches nothing and marks nobody — which is why cancelling is one act too.
